sentences.text:
Petitioner
 Versus
 The State of Jharkhand ...

Opposite Party
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
For the Petitioner : Mr. Anjani Kumar, Adv.
For the State : Mr. Vineet Kr. Vashishta, S. P.P. Order No.04 Dated- 21.07.2022 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

The petitioner has been made accused in connection with Barhi P.S. Case No. 110 of 2013 (G.R.
No.1263 of 2013) registered under sections 414, 467, 468, 471, 420 and 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 33 of Indian Forest Act.
As per FIR, allegation is that petitioner has been made accused in this case for dealing in theft coal on the basis of forged documents.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that nothing has been recovered from the possession of petitioner and he has no concern with seized coal rather he has falsely been implicated in this case only on the basis of confessional statement of co-accused person.

Co-accused Parmeshwar Saw @ Parmeshwar Nayak with similar allegation has already been admitted regular bail by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 19.04.2023 passed in B.A. No.2016 of 2023.

Petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the trial of the case and remain physically present on each and every date till the conclusion of the trial and shall not indulge in tampering with the prosecution evidence or influence the witnesses or gain over them.
It is next submitted that the petitioner has no criminal antecedent.
The petitioner is languishing in judicial custody since 10.05.2023 without any rhymes and reasons.
Hence the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
Learned Addl. P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner.

Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record and period of custody of the petitioner, I am inclined to release the above named petitioner, on bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner named above, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned JMFC, Hazaribag in connection with Barhi P.S.
Case No. 110 of 2013 (G.R. NO.1263 of 2013) with condition that petitioner shall appear physically on each and every date during the trial of case till its conclusion unless his physical appearance is Kedar Saw @ Kedar Nayak vs The State Of Jharkhand ...
